preview: Nirbhay Hanjura shares his interview experience for an internship at Kotak Life, detailing the online assessment and the technical-cum-HR interview round.
content: Kotak Life Interview Experience Nirbhay Hanjura Third Year Information Technology Location - Mumbai After the end of the fifth semester , kotak life came on-campus for the internship process . The online assessment was conducted on a platform called Freshersworld . The test had 60 questions and the duration of the test was 60 minutes. The test consisted of 5 sections . The camera had to be kept on . Section 1 : Aptitude (10 questions) Section 2 : Logical Reasoning (10 questions) Section 3 : Verbal Aptitude (10 questions ) Section 4 : Java(15 questions) -> Fundamentals of java were asked , Most of the questions here were easy , some of them were core concepts of java so if you are new to java you will not be able answer them . Section 5 : Psql (15 questions ) -> Toughest section out of all . Though I was familiar with sql , here the questions were based on cursors , indexing in psql database . I could attempt only 10 /15 and have no idea if they were correct or not . After the test , I was waiting for the shortlist and had no hopes as in the previous company tests I solved questions but still I wasn't shortlisted . But luckily I got shortlisted in Kotak Life . Interview (Only 1 round)(15-25 minutes) Technical + HR : The interviewer was very friendly and asked about me . Questions asked : ●Introduce yourself ●Which domain do you want to work in After asking these questions the interviewer asked questions with respect to my resume . I have a profile of web developer so he asked ●What is node js and why do we use it ? Ans -> Node.js is an open-source and cro-platform runtime environment for executing JavaScript code outside a browser. You need to remember that NodeJS is not a framework and it’s not a programming language. We often use Node.js for building back-end services like APIs like Web App or Mobile App. ●What is react js ? Ans -> The React.js framework is an open-source JavaScript framework and library developed by Facebook. It’s used for building interactive user interfaces and web applications quickly and efficiently with significantly less code than you would with vanilla JavaScript. ●What is npm ? Ans -> npm is two things: first and foremost, it is an online repository for the publishing of open-source Node.js projects; second, it is a command-line utility for interacting with said repository that aids in package installation, and dependency management . Then he asked me questions on fundamentals of java as java is my preferred language Questions asked : ●Can you overload main function in java - > Yes , but there is only one public static void main others cannot be the same . ●Difference between array and arraylist - > Array has a fixed size while the arraylist is dynamic and the interface that implements them are different . ●What is garbage collector in java - > Garbage collection in Java is the process by which Java programs perform automatic memory management. Java programs compile to bytecode that can be run on a Java Virtual Machine, or JVM for short. When Java programs run on the JVM, objects are created on the heap, which is a portion of memory dedicated to the program. Eventually, some objects will no longer be needed. The garbage collector finds these unused objects and deletes them to free up memory. ●How does garbage collector work in java - > By freeing up heap memory . Java garbage collection is an automatic process. Automatic garbage collection is the process of looking at heap memory, identifying which objects are in use and which are not, and deleting the unused objects. An in-use object, or a referenced object, means that some part of your program still maintains a pointer to that object. An unused or unreferenced object is no longer referenced by any part of your program. ●What are unreachable objects in java wrt to garbage collector -> Unreachable objects are the objects which when deleted cannot be dumped properly because they cannot be accessed directly . At last he asked “ Do you have any questions for me “ ? Do ask questions to the interviewer which makes them feel that you are interested Resources : Java fundamentals : https://www.javatpoint.com/java-basics
